2027-06-28.title: Monday of the sixth week after Pentecost · Mar Irenaeus
readings: Avoid wrangling over words; a worker who has no need to be ashamed, rightly explaining the word of truth
“You did not choose me but I chose you”: fruit that will last
2027-06-28.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Sixth Sunday after Pentecost. Today is the last weekday of the Apostles' Fast (Shleeha Nombu), which ends tomorrow with the feast of Sts Peter and Paul. The Panchangam remembers Mar Irenaeus (St Irenaeus of Lyons, bishop, died about 202) and keeps the name day of Most Rev. Samuel Mar Irenaios.
2027-06-28.verse: Do your best to present yourself to God as one approved by him, a worker who has no need to be ashamed, rightly explaining the word of truth.
theo: This is the last weekday of the Apostles' Fast. Tomorrow we keep the feast of Sts Peter and Paul and the fast comes to an end. Today St Paul, writing from prison to his young disciple Timothy, gives advice that every teacher of the faith needs: “Remind them of this, and warn them before God that they are to avoid wrangling over words, which does no good but only ruins those who are listening.” Paul is not against careful thought; he is against the quarrelsome spirit that turns the word of God into a battlefield for pride. Then he gives the positive picture: “Do your best to present yourself to God as one approved by him, a worker who has no need to be ashamed, rightly explaining the word of truth. Avoid profane chatter, for it will lead people into more and more impiety.” The word translated “rightly explaining” describes cutting a straight road or a straight furrow: the teacher's task is to lay the word of truth out straight, so that others can walk on it. Every catechist, every parent who teaches a child to pray, every preacher on Sunday, is called to be such a worker.

The Panchangam today remembers a bishop who did exactly that: Mar Irenaeus, St Irenaeus of Lyons. He was born in Asia Minor in the second century, and as a young man he listened to St Polycarp of Smyrna, who had himself known the Apostle John. Years later Irenaeus wrote to a friend that he could still describe the place where Polycarp sat and talked, and how he told of his conversations with John and with others who had seen the Lord (in Eusebius, Church History 5.20, in substance). Irenaeus went to Gaul, served as a priest in Lyons and, after the martyrdom of Bishop Pothinus in the persecution of 177, became bishop there. In his day groups called Gnostics were wrangling over secret words and hidden teachings, claiming a knowledge higher than the faith of ordinary Christians. Against them Irenaeus wrote his great work Against Heresies. He did not answer with clever speculation; he pointed to the faith handed down openly from the Apostles in the churches through the succession of bishops, and above all to the Church of Rome, which he described as founded and organized by the two most glorious apostles, Peter and Paul (Against Heresies 3.3.2, in substance), the Apostles whose feast we keep tomorrow.

His name means peaceful, and the historian Eusebius remarked that he lived up to it, for when a dispute about the date of Easter threatened to divide the churches, Irenaeus wrote to the Bishop of Rome urging patience and peace (Church History 5.24, in substance). In 2022 Pope Francis declared him a Doctor of the Church with the title Doctor of Unity. Irenaeus also left us one of the most beautiful sayings of the early Church: the glory of God is a human being fully alive, and the life of a human being is the vision of God (Against Heresies 4.20.7, in substance). Tradition honours him as a martyr; he died around the year 202. Today too the Panchangam keeps the name day of Most Rev. Samuel Mar Irenaios. In our tradition a bishop receives a new name at his ordination, and the feast of the saint whose name he bears is kept as his name day. We pray today that he may be, like his patron, a teacher of the true faith and a servant of unity.

The Gospel shows where all this begins. Jesus says to the Apostles: “You did not choose me but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that will last, so that the Father will give you whatever you ask him in my name. I am giving you these commands so that you may love one another.” The Apostles did not apply for the job; they were chosen. The fruit they bore has lasted twenty centuries: John taught Polycarp, Polycarp taught Irenaeus, and the faith came down the generations, through the Apostle Thomas and his successors, to our own land and our own parish. The fruit that lasts is not wrangling but love. On this last day of the fast, let us thank God for those who handed on the faith to us, ask for the grace to explain it straight and live it with love, and prepare our hearts for tomorrow's feast of the two Apostles on whom, as Irenaeus taught, the Church of Rome was founded.
outline: Ask: when I speak about my faith, do I build up or do I quarrel?
Point 1 · Workers with no need to be ashamed
Avoid wrangling over words; lay the word of truth out straight.
Point 2 · Mar Irenaeus, teacher of the apostolic faith
From John to Polycarp to Irenaeus; the faith handed down in the Church, founded on Peter and Paul.
A bishop who lived up to his name; the glory of God is a human being fully alive.
Point 4 · Chosen to bear lasting fruit
The Apostles chosen by Christ, the fruit of love that lasts.
“You did not choose me but I chose you.”
live: Read tomorrow's Gospel of the feast (John 21:15–19) tonight and explain it in simple words to one member of your family.
Refuse to join one argument about religion or the Church this week, online or at home, that only wounds; say a prayer for unity instead.
Thank by name someone who handed on the faith to you, by a call, a visit or a prayer.
2027-06-28.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you chose your Apostles and appointed them to go and bear fruit that will last. Through the prayers of Mar Irenaeus, who received the faith from those who knew your Apostles and defended it with patience and peace, keep your Church in the true faith handed down to us. Make us workers who have no need to be ashamed, rightly explaining the word of truth, and keep us from wrangling over words and from idle talk. Bless our bishop Samuel Mar Irenaios on his name day, and all the shepherds of your Church. As the Apostles' Fast ends, prepare our hearts to celebrate Sts Peter and Paul, and let us bear the fruit of love. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: Irenaeus taught that the bread over which God's name is invoked is no longer common bread but the Eucharist; at every Holy Qurbono the faith of the Apostles is handed on, and the fruit that lasts is given to us as food.
conn: 2 Timothy 2:2: “what you have heard from me through many witnesses entrust to faithful people who will be able to teach others as well”; Irenaeus received the faith from Polycarp, who had known the Apostle John.
John 15:16 describes the choice of the Apostles; the Apostles' Fast, which ends tomorrow, remembers their mission, and Irenaeus is one of its lasting fruits.
Irenaeus wrote that the Church of Rome was founded and organized by Peter and Paul (Against Heresies 3.3.2); their feast is kept tomorrow, 29 June.
fathers: The Church, though spread throughout the whole world, carefully preserves the one faith received from the Apostles and their disciples, as if she lived in one house and had one soul and one mouth (Against Heresies 1.10.2, in substance).
Irenaeus was well named, for in name and in deed he was a peacemaker, pleading for the peace of the churches (Church History 5.24, in substance).

Jesus says: You did not choose me; this is grace that cannot be spoken, for what were we before Christ chose us, if not sinners? He chose us not because we were good, but to make us good (Tractates on John 86, in substance).
magis: Irenaeus taught that the Church, scattered through the whole world, guards the faith received from the Apostles as one family, with one heart and one voice; so the Church's message is true and solid, showing one way of salvation in all the world (in substance).

Particular Churches are fully catholic through their communion with the Church of Rome, which presides in charity; Irenaeus taught that with this Church, because of its superior origin, all the Churches must agree (in substance).
The glory of God consists in the realization of his goodness; as Irenaeus said, the glory of God is a human being fully alive, and the life of a human being is the vision of God (in substance).

quick: Paul tells Timothy to avoid wrangling over words and to be a worker who rightly explains the word of truth.
Mar Irenaeus, who learned the faith from St Polycarp, defended the faith of the Apostles handed down in the Church and worked for peace.
Jesus chose the Apostles and appointed them to bear fruit that will last, and commanded them to love one another.
2027-06-28.action: Thank God today, by name, for the people who handed on the faith to you.
2027-06-28.question: Do I help others to understand the faith, or do I only argue about it?

family.explain: Jesus chose his Apostles and sent them to tell everyone about God's love. They taught others, and those taught others again, like a long chain of hands passing on a lamp. St Irenaeus, whom we remember today, learned about Jesus from an old bishop, St Polycarp, who had known the Apostle John. Our parents and grandparents are part of that chain too, and now we are.
family.intention: We pray for our bishop Samuel Mar Irenaios on his name day, and for all who teach the faith.
family.ask: Ask: “Who taught me to pray? Let us thank God for that person tonight.”

illus: A catechism teacher in a small parish near Mavelikkara retired after teaching the Sunday class for forty years. At her farewell, the parish priest asked those in the church who had learned their prayers from her to stand up. Grandfathers stood, and their sons, and their grandchildren; the young assistant priest stood, and so did two religious sisters who were visiting their families. Almost the whole church was on its feet. The old teacher could not speak. When she finally took the microphone, she said only this: I learned the Our Father from my grandmother, who learned it from hers. I did not teach you anything of my own. I only passed it on as straight as I could.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you chose us and sent us to bear fruit that will last. Through the prayers of Mar Irenaeus, keep us in the faith of the Apostles, in peace and in love. Amen.
share: Avoid wrangling over words, which does no good (2 Timothy 2:14). Where do I quarrel when I should build up?
A worker who has no need to be ashamed, rightly explaining the word of truth (2 Timothy 2:15). How well do I know and explain my faith?
You did not choose me but I chose you (John 15:16). How does it change my life to know that Christ chose me?
pm.resp: Lord, keep us in the faith of your Apostles.
interc: For the Church, that she may guard the faith received from the Apostles with one heart and one voice.
For Most Rev. Samuel Mar Irenaios on his name day, and for all our bishops, that they may be teachers of the truth and servants of unity.
For catechists, teachers and parents who hand on the faith, that they may explain the word of truth rightly.
For an end to quarrels and divisions among Christians, that all may be one.
For all who have kept the Apostles' Fast, that they may celebrate the feast of Sts Peter and Paul with renewed faith.
pm.close: Father, you gave Mar Irenaeus the grace to guard the faith of the Apostles and to work for peace. Keep your Church faithful to the teaching she has received, united in charity, and fruitful in every good work. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: The feast of the saint whose name a person bears. In the Syro-Malankara Church, as in other Syriac Churches, a bishop receives a new name at his episcopal ordination, usually the name of a saint or Father of the Church preceded by the title Mar; the feast of that saint is kept as his name day, and the faithful pray for him on that day.
kidsaint: When Irenaeus was a boy, he loved to sit and listen to an old bishop named Polycarp. Polycarp told stories about the Apostle John, who had been Jesus' friend. Many years later, when Irenaeus was himself an old bishop, he wrote that he could still remember the very place where Polycarp sat and the way he spoke. Lesson: listen carefully to the people who tell you about Jesus. One day you will pass it on too.

homily: Dear friends, today is the last weekday of the Apostles' Fast, and tomorrow we celebrate Sts Peter and Paul. St Paul writes to Timothy: avoid wrangling over words, which does no good but only ruins those who are listening (2 Timothy 2:14). Instead, be a worker who has no need to be ashamed, rightly explaining the word of truth (2 Timothy 2:15). Quarrels about words destroy; the truth explained with love builds up.

Today we remember Mar Irenaeus. As a young man he listened to St Polycarp, who had known the Apostle John. He became bishop of Lyons and defended the faith against people who invented secret teachings. He told them: look at the faith handed down in the Church from the Apostles, and especially in the Church of Rome founded on Peter and Paul. His name means peaceful, and he worked for peace among the churches. We also pray today for our bishop Samuel Mar Irenaios on his name day.

In the Gospel Jesus tells the Apostles: You did not choose me but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that will last (John 15:16). The fruit has lasted: from John to Polycarp to Irenaeus, and down to us. And Jesus tells us what that fruit is: I am giving you these commands so that you may love one another (John 15:17).

So let us thank God for those who handed on the faith to us. Let us learn our faith well, so that we can explain it straight. Let us avoid quarrels that wound, and let us prepare our hearts for tomorrow's feast. Amen.
kids: Children, have you ever played the game where you whisper a message from one person to the next? Sometimes the message gets mixed up! Jesus gave his message to the Apostles, and they passed it on very carefully. St Irenaeus learned it from Polycarp, who learned it from the Apostle John. And it came all the way to us, through our parents and teachers. Listen well when you learn about Jesus, so that you can pass the message on without mixing it up.

intro: Theme: “You did not choose me but I chose you.”

On Monday of the sixth week after Pentecost, the last weekday of the Apostles' Fast, with Mar Irenaeus and the name day of Most Rev. Samuel Mar Irenaios: workers who rightly explain the word of truth, the apostolic faith handed down, the peacemaker, and the fruit that lasts.

points.h: Workers with no need to be ashamed
sub: Cutting the word of truth straight.
Every parent and catechist a worker.
q: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
All scripture is inspired by God and is useful for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness,
points.apply: Learn one article of the Creed well this week, so that you can explain it to a child.

points.h: Mar Irenaeus and the apostolic faith
sub: From John to Polycarp to Irenaeus.
The faith handed down openly, not secret knowledge.
The Church of Rome, founded on Peter and Paul.
q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
making every effort to maintain the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
points.apply: Pray tomorrow, on the feast of the Apostles, for the Pope and for the unity of all Christians.

sub: Not chosen because we were good, but to make us good.
The fruit of love that lasts.
Praying for our bishops on their name days.
q: They are like trees planted by streams of water, which yield their fruit in its season, and their leaves do not wither.
By contrast, the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, generosity, faithfulness,
points.apply: Thank by name someone who handed on the faith to you.

concl: The faith of the Apostles has come to us through a chain of faithful teachers, and Irenaeus is one of its strongest links.
Christ chose us to bear the fruit that lasts: truth explained rightly and lived in love.
2027-06-28.resolve: Learn the faith, hand it on straight, avoid quarrels that wound, and bear the fruit of love.
